proposals.rule: Always include test cases where wide-selector inputs (e.g., sel) are set to powers of two and to values just above and below each power‑of‑two boundary.
proposals.summary: Add rule to stimulate edge‑case selector values for wide‑input multiplexers.
proposals.reasoning: Many missed bugs involve wide‑input muxes where the selector indexes into a packed vector (e.g., Prob021_mux256to1v). Testing selector values that are powers of two and adjacent values exercises the boundary conditions where off‑by‑one errors in index calculation manifest.

proposals.summary: Add static analysis tool that flags designs where shift or index expressions could exceed the width of an input port.
proposals.reasoning: Several missed bugs stem from shift/index calculations that can overflow the input width (e.g., Prob021_mux256to1v, Prob054_edgedetect). A tool that statically detects such potential overflows will give the attacker hints to generate targeted stimuli.

proposals.summary: Double the maximum cycles allowed for stimulus generation from 40 to 80.
proposals.reasoning: Increasing the cycle budget enables longer sequences needed to trigger bugs that require multiple clock cycles to manifest (e.g., Prob080_timer, Prob140_fsm_hdlc). Past attempts showed that more cycles can uncover additional mismatches without overly burdening the search.
